sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173 of the Motors Vehicle Act against the award dated 17.01.2022 passed by 3rd Additional Member to the Court of 1st Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni in Claim Case No.448/2019, whereby learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,11384/-.
2.

entities.text: Court of 1st Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Short question involved in the present appeal is with regard to enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, facts related to the accident etc. are not being reproduced/
discussed.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has not awarded sufficient amount for compensation.
It is submitted that due to the accident, appellant has received several injuries and fractures.
He was admitted to the Hospital from 09.07.2018 to 15.08.2018 where he was operated and steel rod was inserted in his leg.
As per permanent disability certificate of the appellant, it was 10% for the wounded area and 6% for the whole body.
It is also submitted that due to the said accident, appellant suffered fractures over Humerus Bone and Radius Bone of left hand and Femur Bone of left thigh.

It is further submitted that the appellant used to work as Mason and for this occupation use of hands and legs are of vital importance and due to fractures he cannot perform his work as he used to perform previously therefore, loss of income should calculated 6%.

It is also submitted that learned Tribunal has determined income of the injured on the lower side whereas the income of injured should have been determined on the basis of notification issued under Minimum Wages Act, 1948.
In view of the above submission, appeal be allowed and compensation be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 Insurance Company submits that the compensation awarded by Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. From perusal of record, it is found that appellant sustained injuries on his hands and legs.
He was admitted to the hospital where he was operated.
In permanent disability certificate, total 6% of disability is ascertained for his whole body.
He used to work as Manson and for this occupation use of hands and legs are of vital importance.

Therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court loss of income injured should be calculated at 5%.
7.
So far as income of appellant is concerned, learned Tribunal, in para No.41 of the award, has determined monthly income of the appellant as Rs.6000/-.

It is well settled that if there is no proof of income of appellant or otherwise from evidence on record, income of appellant is not proved,
then, the same should be determined on the basis of minimum wages fixed as per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948.

Present accident relates to the year, 2018 and minimum wages fixed for unskilled labour for above year is Rs.7,325/- per month. Appellant - claimant would also be entitled for compensation under the head of "future prospect" @ 40%.
8.
There is no dispute with regard to the fact that appellant - claimant was between the age group of 31-35 years.

In view of the above as well as in the light of case law of National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.; 2017 ACJ 2700, considering the annual income of the claimant to be Rs.87,900/-
(Rs.7,325 x 12), multiplier of 16, loss of future earning capacity @ 5%, future prospect @ 40%,
Rs.21,975/- towards loss of income during the period appellant remained admitted and was treated,
Rs.25,000/- towards physical pain and suffering and Rs.20,000/- towards mental pain and suffering, Rs.20,000/- for nutritious diet, Rs.20,000/- for attender expenses total compensation amount comes to Rs.2,05,423/- [Rs.70,320 (87,900 x 16 x 5%) 28,128 (40% future prospect on Rs.70,320) 21,975 25,000 20,000 20,000 20,000].

sentences.text:
The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,11,384/-
to the claimant.
The enhanced amount comes to Rs. 94,039/- (Rupees Ninety Four Thousand and Thirty Nine only).
The enhanced amount of compensation i.e. Rs.94,039/- s hall carry interest as awarded by learned claims tribunal from the date of claim application till realization.
The enhanced amount of compensation shall be payable to the appellant - claimant by the Insurance Company within a period of 12 weeks from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
Rest of the award passed by learned claims tribunal shall remain intact.
10. Present miscellaneous appeal is disposed of in above terms.
Records of the learned Claims Tribunal be sent back.
